MATA is a specialized career and technical education program within the Academies of Loudoun. MATA offers programs like biomedical technology, auto-collision, and cosmetology, each designed to give students professional-level training in a specific field. These pathways are either one year or two years in length.

Students spend six hours every other day inside a single specialized program. Let me put that in perspective. In a course in one's homeschool, a student accumulates roughly 128 hours of instruction over the course of a single academic year. On the other hand, one year in a MAD pathway totals approximately 540 hours.

A two-year pathway, like biomedical technology, totals to around 1,080 hours, nearly nine times the instructional time of a course taken at homeschools. This time commitment exists for a reason. All MATA pathways send their students off with collegiate level skills, with some even having end of course certifications, which include CNA or an HVAC certification.

These skill sets allow students to directly carry their qualifications in the workforce the moment they graduate high school. Opportunities like that don't exist in most of the county. So when we talk about MATA, we're talking about half of a student's high school career dedicated to a single professional pathway.
